functionalObligations.text: PayPal is not the issuer: PYUSD is issued by Paxos Trust Company, N.A., and PayPal's own 10-Q calls Paxos 'a third-party issuer (the PYUSD Issuer)' and states the claim precisely -- each token of PYUSD held by PayPal represents a contractual right to redeem with the third-party issuer of PYUSD for one U.S. dollar.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. No symbol for an obligor. The brand-versus-obligor split is the same fact pattern as USD1 (World Liberty Financial owns the brand, BitGo Bank & Trust owes the money) and is unrepresentable in both.

functionalObligations.text: The obligor is not the counterparty: a PayPal or Venmo consumer's counterparty is PayPal under PayPal's user agreement, while the obligor of last resort is Paxos under Paxos's stablecoin terms -- two hops, two contracts, one token.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, new -- not in the corpus. There is no symbol for an INTERMEDIATED CLAIM: a holder whose legal counterparty is a distributor standing between them and the issuer. This is a different structure from USDT's 819 direct customers and from USDC's two-tier terms, because here the intermediary is itself the dominant venue for the instrument.

functionalObligations.text: For a US consumer PYUSD lives inside PayPal's or Venmo's custodial ledger and converts one-for-one to a PayPal balance; moving it on-chain at all requires being 'provisioned for external transfers' and passing PayPal's sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and an unusual gate: every other Aw in this category gates ENTRY to issuance or redemption; this one gates EXIT FROM THE CUSTODIAL LEDGER ONTO THE CHAIN. Aw names an on-chain permission; this is a provisioning flag in a company database that decides whether the token behaves like a token. CORPUS DEPARTURE: Aw is ADDED, on the corpus's own USDC reasoning, and here there are two such gates -- PayPal provisioning for external transfer, and Paxos Platform onboarding for institutional mint and redeem (F5).

functionalObligations.text: The dominant use path never touches a blockchain: most PYUSD activity is a row change in PayPal's or Venmo's custodial database, and the token contract is a settlement layer for a payment network whose real ledger is invisible to it.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the sharpest instance in the whole category. There is no symbol for AN OFF-CHAIN LEDGER THAT SHADOWS THE TOKEN. Corroborated at a primary source rather than inferred: PayPal's 10-Q says on-chain sending requires provisioning, which is a statement that the on-chain representation is an opt-in feature of an off-chain product. Every element in a construction of PYUSD describes the minority of its behaviour.

functionalObligations.text: Direct redemption with the issuer is for institutional users who complete Paxos Platform onboarding -- the issuer 'may also allow institutional users to directly purchase PYUSD from the PYUSD Issuer' -- with the minimum, fee and settlement time not stated in any source reachable at the access date.
functionalObligations.note: BOTH APPROXIMATE. Minimums, fees and settlement times for direct Paxos redemption are UNKNOWN and are not repaired from secondary sources. Rd is doubly strained here: the consumer's practical redemption is a 1:1 conversion inside PayPal's ledger against PayPal, while the contractual redemption right runs against Paxos and is reachable only by institutions. Two different redemptions with two different counterparties, one symbol, and the one the vocabulary is describing is the one almost no holder uses.

functionalObligations.text: Reserves are US dollar deposits, US treasuries and cash equivalents held in segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts at a national trust bank.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The composition is stated only at this level of generality, and the attested per-month figures are UNKNOWN in this record: the report PDFs are served through a JavaScript viewer that stage 1 could not resolve to direct URLs even under a rendered browser fetch. So for two of the five members -- PYUSD and USDG, both Paxos-issued -- the model carries At while the numbers it points at are not retrievable. No bank is named.

functionalObligations.text: Assurance is a two-document regime: monthly attestations by KPMG LLP under AICPA attestation standards for reports posted on or after 2025-02-28 and by WithumSmith+Brown, PC before that date, PLUS a separate self-reported portfolio composition published five business days after month-end that is expressly not subjected to independent review.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://www.paxos.com/pyusd-transparency (accessed 2026-08-04, content read via a rendered browser fetch)
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a regime the corpus does not record. The MORE DETAILED document is the UN-REVIEWED one. At is a single predicate and cannot express that an issuer publishes two documents about the same reserve at different assurance levels, nor that a reader comparing issuers on 'detail of disclosure' is rewarded for reading the one nobody signed. Against law L27: named attester yes, independence yes, stated assurance yes for one document and NONE for the other, no staleness bound, no recourse.

functionalObligations.text: The issuer's own publications do not agree on who supervises it: paxos.com/pyusd states the issuer is Paxos Trust Company, N.A. subject to strict regulatory oversight by the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, while the PYUSD transparency page still describes 'Paxos' prudential regulator, the New York State Department of Financial Services' and its Dollar-Backed Stablecoins guidance as the body approving the examiner's appointment.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. CORPUS CORRECTION: the corpus says 'issued by Paxos Trust under NYDFS'. The consistent reading of the primary sources is that the issuer converted from a New York trust company to a national trust bank under OCC supervision during 2026 and one Paxos page is stale, but WHICH ONE, AND THE EFFECTIVE DATE, ARE UNKNOWN. Both are recorded. A stablecoin whose supervising authority cannot be read consistently off two pages of the issuer's own website is a fact about At's ENVIRONMENT that At cannot hold, and no symbol names a regulator or what it may order.

functionalObligations.text: A second regulator sits over the distributor rather than the issuer: PayPal is regulated by NYDFS as a virtual currency business and is a digital asset service provider under the GENIUS Act.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two supervised entities on one instrument, supervised for different things by different authorities, and the model has no place for either.

functionalObligations.text: An asset-protection authority may freeze and destroy any balance: ASSET_PROTECTION_ROLE holds freeze(address), freezeBatch(address[]), unfreeze, unfreezeBatch and wipeFrozenAddress(address), all present in the verified implementation ABI, with isFrozen(address) a public view.
functionalObligations.note: CANDIDATE REGISTER, used with a note. PYUSD can freeze and destroy and CANNOT forcibly re-assign; USD1 can do all three; USDT can freeze and destroy; USDC can only freeze. Fz names all four. Note the batch forms: freezeBatch and unfreezeBatch make mass action a single transaction, which is an operational property of the power that no element records.

functionalObligations.text: A pause authority may halt all transfers: PAUSE_ROLE holds pause() and unpause(), both present in the verified implementation ABI; paused() reads false at 2026-08-04.
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE: Gp is ADDED. Verified in the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04. With this the corpus's PYUSD-subset-of-USDC claim loses one of the two symbols that made it a strict subset.

functionalObligations.text: Issuance destinations are whitelisted and issuance is rate-limited on-chain: increaseSupply, increaseSupplyToAddress, decreaseSupply, decreaseSupplyFromAddress, mint and burn are all mediated by a separate SupplyControl contract at 0x31d9BDeA6f104606c954f8FE6bA614F1bd347Ec3, reached through supplyControl(), carrying the same per-controller RateLimit and mint-address whitelist design as USDG.
functionalObligations.note: Aw is FIRM for the whitelist half (an on-chain predicate on issuance destination). The RATE LIMIT half is RESIDUE: no element names a quantity-and-rate-bounded issuance authority. See the USDG record F5 -- this is the third independent lane arrival at the bounded-delegate-mandate schema (named agent, domain whitelist, magnitude cap, rate-of-change limit, revocation), here on issuance, and the corpus records it for neither Paxos token.

functionalObligations.text: The token is a ZeppelinOS-style proxy at 0x6c3ea9036406852006290770BEdFcAbA0e23A0e8 with implementation PYUSD at 0x8C35caA5FD5bDc64b6b11344ad57594A3676256a, solc 0.8.28, fully verified 2026-02-09, whose proxy admin 0xc94BcF6E1d8b3558e3b62E743630D50497e3851C is an externally owned account with no code.
functionalObligations.note: Firm fit, with the same X9 question as USDC: Tg is ABSENT, law L15 (Up -> Tg | bounded emergency process) is NOT satisfied, and a single EOA can replace the implementation with no delay. The corpus records armedProhibitions: [] and never computed it against this. Source is MIT at github.com/paxosglobal/pyusd-contract with audits by Trail of Bits (v1) and Zellic and Trail of Bits (PaxosTokenV2); no byte-for-byte repo-to-deployment comparison performed, and no release tag surfaced.

functionalObligations.text: The token's default admin -- which holds reclaimToken(), setSupplyControl() and role administration -- is a bare externally owned account, owner() equal to defaultAdmin() equal to 0x3aF3E85f4f97DE7Ad0F000B724fB77Fe5FFc024b, and the only delay in the system, defaultAdminDelay() of 10800 seconds, applies to TRANSFERRING that role and not to using it.
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com eth_call owner(), defaultAdmin(), defaultAdminDelay() at 0x6c3ea9036406852006290770BEdFcAbA0e23A0e8 and eth_getCode at 0x3aF3E85f4f97DE7Ad0F000B724fB77Fe5FFc024b (accessed 2026-08-04) | https://eth.blockscout.com/api/v2/smart-contracts/0x8c35caa5fd5bdc64b6b11344ad57594a3676256a (accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and Tg is deliberately NOT ASSIGNED. defaultAdminDelay is NOT a timelock: it delays who the admin is, not what the admin does. USDG has both delays (86400 on actions, 10800 on handover); PYUSD has only the second. Assigning Tg here would make the two Paxos tokens look alike on precisely the axis where they differ most -- and that axis is the single sharpest governance difference in the category. Up cannot distinguish 'the key acts slowly' from 'the key acts instantly but changes hands slowly', and this is the instance that proves it matters.

functionalObligations.text: PYUSD shares the Paxos implementation base with USDG -- PaxosTokenV2 over BaseStorage, EIP2612, EIP3009 and AccessControlDefaultAdminRulesUpgradeable, with the same SupplyControl and RateLimit machinery -- but has NO rewards module and NO facet router.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Two tokens from one issuer on one code base differ by a rewards ledger, a facet router and a timelock, and the model's only way to state the relation between them is to compare element sets after the fact. The intents and yield lanes found the same gap between protocols (containment is inexpressible); here it appears between two instruments sharing a repository, which is the strongest form of it -- the shared base is a fact about the artefacts, and constructions are stated over behaviours.

functionalObligations.text: A holder may authorise transfers by signature: the implementation exposes EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, receiveWithAuthorization and cancelAuthorization, EIP-2612 permit, and transferFromBatch.
functionalObligations.note: APPROXIMATE, and a NEW ASSIGNMENT the corpus codes for none of the five. Law L17's four terms are satisfied exactly (bounded scope, cancelAuthorization, validAfter/validBefore, nonce under an EIP-712 domain); approximate only against Au's 'session policy' gloss, this being single-shot delegation. Verified from the implementation ABI on 2026-08-04. NOTE ITS LOAD: Au is the ONLY element separating PYUSD's construction from USDT's. Without it the two are set-identical, and the difference it names is that PYUSD's 2024 code post-dates two EIPs that USDT's 2018 Solidity 0.4.18 code pre-dates -- a fact about compiler eras, not about what makes either token worth a dollar.

functionalObligations.text: PYUSD is deployed on five documented mainnets -- Ethereum, Solana, Arbitrum, Polygon PoS and X Layer -- each with its own token contract AND its own Supply Control contract address, which is the signature of independent native issuance rather than a bridged representation.
functionalObligations.note: CORPUS DEPARTURE, and the one this lane was asked to make with care: Xf and Xm are REMOVED. The corpus's Xm marker asserts that 'the LayerZero OFT deployment to Solana/Arbitrum is genuine cross-domain messaging'. NO PRIMARY PAXOS STATEMENT OF A LAYERZERO PATH FOR PYUSD WAS FOUND, and the documented picture -- five chains, each with its own token and its own supply controller -- is the signature of native per-chain issuance. Either the corpus is citing a distinct product (PYUSD0) or the claim is stale. Marked UNCONFIRMED in stage 1 and NOT CARRIED here, because carrying a cross-domain mechanism on an unverified premise is exactly the forced fit the contract forbids. The consequence is stated plainly in F18.

functionalObligations.text: With the cross-domain elements withdrawn, PYUSD's on-chain behaviour reduces to transfer accounting, a permission gate on issuance, a freeze-and-wipe power, a pause, a signed-authorisation family and an upgradeable implementation behind a single key.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, recorded as an obligation because the collapse is itself the finding stage 1 predicted. PYUSD's construction {At, Au, Aw, Fz, Gp, Rd, Up} is a strict superset of USDT's {At, Aw, Fz, Gp, Rd, Up} by exactly one element, Au (F16). Two systems with different obligors, different charters, different reserves, different creditor positions and different seizure powers are separated by whether their compiler era supported EIP-3009. If a stage-3 auditor rejects Au as a forced fit, PYUSD and USDT become SET-IDENTICAL and the category carries three identical pairs rather than one. Either way the finding stands: the vocabulary's resolution in this category is not merely coarse, it discriminates on the wrong axis.

functionalObligations.text: PayPal pays a variable-rate PYUSD reward to eligible US users who hold a PYUSD balance in the PayPal app, funded by PayPal as distributor rather than by Paxos as issuer or by any on-chain protocol.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Em rejected (not protocol emissions), Fd rejected (not a surplus distribution by the issuer -- it is marketing spend by the distributor), Ix and Sr rejected (the accrual is a field in PayPal's ledger). The contrast with USDG is the sharpest available test of the vocabulary's boundary: an economically similar payment IS partly on-chain there and earns Fd, Sh and Ep; here the same economics earn nothing. SAME ECONOMICS, DIFFERENT OBSERVABILITY, AND THE VOCABULARY SEES ONE AND NOT THE OTHER. The rate at 2026-08-04 is UNKNOWN from a dated primary quotation and is not carried.

functionalObligations.text: The same instrument is reversible on one side of the custodial boundary and final on the other: dispute reversal and chargeback exist as primitives in PayPal's ledger and cannot exist in the token.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. Nothing in the model can express an instrument whose FINALITY DEPENDS ON WHICH LEDGER YOU ARE LOOKING AT. The corpus names chargeback semantics as residue; the sharper statement is that the wrapper must support a forced reversal the token cannot, so the consumer product and the on-chain product are different instruments that share a unit of account.

functionalObligations.text: PayPal itself holds PYUSD on its own balance sheet, carried at amortised cost and classified alongside cash and cash equivalents.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. The distributor is also a holder, and a large one, and its accounting treatment of the instrument is a public statement about what it believes the instrument is. No element names a party's position in the token it distributes, nor the reflexivity that follows.

functionalObligations.text: On-chain the token is plain balance accounting: 6 decimals and Ethereum supply 1,832,790,045.376448 at 2026-08-04, against the corpus's US$2.68B all-chain figure.
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, as at USDT F12: Sh, Ix and Rb name three ways a claim's value can move and none names a claim whose value does not move. The attested outstanding could not be retrieved (F6), so the on-chain Ethereum leg is the only figure this record can assert, and it is 68% of the corpus's all-chain number.

paper.title: PayPal USD
paper.label: cat:fiat:pyusd
paper.blurb: An issuer whose token is a thin contract over a large regulated arrangement, and whose supervisory regime changed during the period the corpus covers.
paper.witnessReason: The witness removes the cross-domain elements the element-set decomposition assigns, because no primary source supports them for this issuer. Removing an unsupported element is the same discipline as adding a supported one, and it is what makes the remaining identity claims in this category mean anything.
paper.residueNote: This issuer shares its freeze key with another in the same category, held by one account. Two issuers with different obligors, different regulators and different reserves have a single common point of control, and the model has no way to say so.
